assumptions_note: SIMULATION MODEL, not observed data. Conversion probabilities are authored assumptions, loosely shaped by publicly discussed industry retry/recovery rates: matched interventions convert meaningfully better than blind retries, second attempts convert worse than first, and nudges on true abandonment outperform retries on hard declines. Every batch number in this project derived from these values is labelled simulated. One recovery in the repo is observed for real via a test-mode payment link paid with a test card; it is flagged observed:true in the ledger.
repeat_action_note: Attempt 2 decays differently depending on whether it REPEATS the action that just failed. Re-firing an action the customer already ignored or that the issuer already rejected should not retain most of its original power, so repeat_action_decay is much harsher than second_attempt_decay. STATED BIAS: the baseline policy always re-fires retry_same_cooldown, so it takes the harsher decay on every second attempt by construction, while the agent takes it only when it deliberately repeats. This widens the agent-vs-baseline gap. We consider that the correct modelling of blind retry rather than a thumb on the scale, but it is an authored assumption and is called out here so the delta can be discounted by anyone who disagrees. Setting repeat_action_decay equal to second_attempt_decay reproduces the previous, neutral behaviour.
